info.bio: Siouxsie & the Banshees es el nombre de una banda de rock británica formada en 1976. La banda liderada por Siouxsie fue uno de los grupos claves de la música de los años 80. Abanderados del movimiento post-punk, su música continuó evolucionando. El grupo se disolvió en 1996, aunque se volvió a juntar brevemente para una gira en 2002. La cantante también creó un segundo grupo The Creatures en 1981, con el que paralelamente continuó su carrera y con el que continuó después de la disolución de los banshees.

own_scenes.desc: Fans de Roxy Music que no creían en el igualitarismo punk («No todo el mundo puede hacerlo»): minimalismo por descarte (sin solos, sin finales de batería), guitarra con flanger entre la Velvet y la ducha de Psicosis, la voz gélida de Siouxsie y letras antisentimentales sobre la locura y los suburbios («Suburban Relapse», «Jigsaw Feeling»). The Scream (1978), Join Hands («Icon», el padrenuestro), Kaleidoscope con John McGeoch y Budgie, Juju (1981), su obra cumbre y matriz del gótico (magia, vudú, Halloween), y A Kiss in the Dreamhouse (1982), decadencia fin de siglo y psicodelia inglesa. Siouxsie quería ser «un palo en la rueda de la mediocridad».

refs.q: La cantante de The Banshees, Siouxsie Sioux, retrató perfectamente el espíritu del naciente movimiento gótico
refs.para: La cantante de The Banshees, Siouxsie Sioux, retrató perfectamente el espíritu del naciente movimiento gótico cuando declaró que quería ser "un palo en la rueda de la mediocridad". Al comienzo, sin embargo, The Banshees eran los clásicos músicos postpunk vanguardistas que creían que el rock estaba muerto y cosa5 por el estilo. El bajista, Steve Severin, afirmó que el rock era "flácido y pervertido", y en entrevistas citaba como influencias a artistas parecidos a los que mencionaban sus contemporáneos: The Velvet Underground, Roxy Music, Can, Captain Beefheart.
refs.chapter: Cap. 21: Oscuridad y juventud gloriosa: el regreso del rock con el gótico y la nueva psicodelia

refs.q: Siouxsie quería que la guitarra sonara como "una mezcla entre The Velvet Underground y la escena de la ducha de Psicosis"
refs.para: Siouxsie quería que la guitarra sonara como "una mezcla entre The Velvet Underground y la escena de la ducha de Psicosis", según Severin. Al principio, los críticos emparentaban a la banda con Wire, que también cultivaba una suerte de minimalismo abstracto. Asimismo, ambos grupos eran fanáticos del flanger, un efecto de guitarra con un sonido muy delicado, creado por un aparato que duplica la señal sonora y luego ubica la segunda señal ligeramente desfasada respecto de la primera. The Banshees lo utilizaba para distanciarse lo más posible del rock de los setenta. En su primer álbum, The Scream, editado en 1 978, el resultado era una sonoridad casi opuesta a la del rock tradicional, un nuevo estilo cruel y geométrico construido con y contra el formato ortodoxo del género: guitarra, bajo y batería.
refs.chapter: Cap. 21: Oscuridad y juventud gloriosa: el regreso del rock con el gótico y la nueva psicodelia

refs.q: Sin embargo, Juju, de 198 1, es la obra cumbre de la banda
refs.para: Después de ciertos cambios en la formación (tanto el baterista Kenny Morris como el guitarrista John McKay se fueron del grupo), The Banshees agregaron a otro guitarrista más técnico y convencional, John McGeoch (ex integrante de Magazine), y al baterista Budgie para la grabación de Kaleidoscope. Como indica el nombre, el álbum marcó una transición del rigor monocromático de los primeros dos discos a una paleta más variada de colores. La banda incluso logró un sonido encantador en singles como "Christine" y "Happy House", temas que fueron bits en Gran Bretaña. Sin embargo, Juju, de 198 1, es la obra cumbre de la banda: cada canción parece esculpida con el mismo material os- curo e impecable. El álbum definió muchísimos aspectos líricos y musicales de lo que sería el gótico. En "Sin in My Heart", "Voodoo Dolly", "Halloween", "Spellbound" y "Night Shift", la banda exploró por primera vez ideas relacionadas con la magia y lo sobrenatural.

scenes.name: Dark punk y rock gótico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk británico estuvo flanqueado desde el principio por un movimiento «gótico» que canalizaba su violencia hacia atmósferas de terror y rituales esotéricos: Stranglers, Siouxsie, X-Ray Spex. Lo más interesante evita el tono de película de terror: The Cure introducen la angustia existencial de Camus y Sartre (Pornography, Disintegration); Joy Division mezclan Doors, Kraftwerk y Black Sabbath y su final anuncia el synth-pop; Bauhaus, Killing Joke, Psychedelic Furs, los irlandeses Virgin Prunes y la cima del género, Public Image Ltd de Johnny Lydon, que convierte el punk en música de cámara con dub y ecos étnicos (Second Edition, Flowers Of Romance). Después, el gótico bailable de Sisters Of Mercy, Alien Sex Fiend, Cult, Mission e In The Nursery.

Esa conno-tación negativa duró hasta fines de 1 982, cuando la palabra fue adoptada como estandarte por los mismos seguidores de esas bandas. La…

podcast.title: Debut Performance – September 1976
podcast.body: The band made its debut performance in September 1976 with Sid Vicious on drums. Susan Ballion, who later reinvented herself as Siouxsie Sioux, was the vocalist. "He was the drummer for Susie in the Banshees when they made their debut in September of 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Debut at 100 Club (1976)
podcast.body: This new group made its debut at the 100 Club Punk Rock Festival on September 20, 1976. On the first night, their drummer savagely beat up a well-known music journalist, and on the second night, the same individual was arrested for throwing a beer glass, blinding a girl in one eye. This drummer was Sid Vicious, who would later join the Sex Pistols. "The lineup featured a new group called The Clash, a group making their debut called Susie in the Band Sheets, the Buzzcocks were there around a few others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Lineup
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza festival in the summer of 1991.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, contributing to the festival's success despite initial ticket struggles, and helping to demonstrate the demand for non-mainstream music. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Performance (1991)
podcast.body: Suzy and the Banshees were part of the diverse roster of bands performing at the first Lollapalooza festival in 1991, an event designed to introduce a broad range of alternative music to a wider American audience. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Breakup (1996)
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the bandsheets officially broke up in 1996. "even though the group broke up in 1996."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accused of Being "Too Pop"
podcast.body: Siouxsie was later accused by some within the Goth scene of becoming "too pop" for the genre. "Sousing the banshees and the cure out front, although Susie would later be accused of being too pop for Goth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Aligned with Ian Curtis
podcast.body: Martin Hannett's innovative production ideas for Joy Division's sound were well-received and strongly aligned with Ian Curtis's artistic vision, particularly with the themes explored in Curtis's lyrics. This alignment contributed to creative tensions within the band, as other members, like Peter Hook, preferred a rawer, more aggressive sound. "Martin Hannett que está embujando la banda y que Ian Kurt y centrarían muy bien a esas ideas que estaba introduciendo Martin Hannett."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Association with Goth Culture
podcast.body: The band is recognized as one of the founders of modern goth culture, a label they reportedly disliked but from which they are inseparable within the scene. Siouxsie Sue is frequently considered the "queen of Goth" by many fans. "The bandsheets were one of the founders of modern goth culture. And even though they hated that tag, they are inseparable from that scene. Susie is still considered to be the queen of Goth by many fans"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bill Grundy TV Incident
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux was the woman on whom Bill Grundy made advances during the famous and controversial TV episode involving the Sex Pistols. "In fact, if you've ever seen or heard the famous Bill Grundy TV episode with the pistols, the woman Grundy hits on is, in fact, Suzy Su."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bromley Contingent Member
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux was a member of the Bromley Contingent, a group of fans who consistently followed the Sex Pistols to their gigs. "Singer Suzy Su was a member of a group of fans called the Bromley Contention, who followed the sex pistols around from gig to gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Steve Lillywhite
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were among the many notable bands and artists with whom British producer Steve Lillywhite worked on albums. "Steve Lilley White, the British producer who worked on albums from You Too, The Psychedelic Furs, Peter Gabriel Simple Minds, Talking Heads, Morrissey, Rolling Stones, Dave Matthews, BDI, The Killer, Suzing the Banshees, and dozens more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stop Me If You've Heard This One Before

podcast.title: Contemporaries of Pulp
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were forming almost simultaneously with Pulp, positioning Pulp's origins in the same early post-punk scene as these influential bands. "Palt was forming almost at the same time as groups like Joy Division or like Suixion de Bansis then."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Creators of Heavy, Melancholic Atmospheres
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees (likely "Sips and the Abansis" in the transcript) were among the "darks" who created heavy and melancholic atmospheres in music, influenced by literary figures like Kafka, Dostoevsky, and Baudelaire. "Sips and the Abansis... Y creaban atmósferas pesadas y melancólicas."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La traición que salvó al punk. PiL

podcast.title: Early Performance with Sid Vicious
podcast.body: On September 20, 1976, Sid Vicious played drums for a very early version of Siouxsie and the Banshees at the 100 Club Punk Special, where the group improvised interminably on the Lord's Prayer. "On September 20th, 1976, Sid somehow ended up playing drums for a very early version of Suzy in the Banshees at a two-day punk event called the 100 Club Punk Special."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

podcast.title: Featured on 80s US New Wave Compilations
podcast.body: In the 1980s, compilations edited as "New Wave" in the United States often featured a diverse range of British bands, including Siouxsie and the Banshees, reflecting how the term was applied to non-mainstream UK music. "Incluso los ex Tisí y los culturclava, vean como New Wave, muchos recominatorios en Estados Unidos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: First Post-Punk Association
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees are strongly associated with the term "post-punk," with their 1977 single "Hong Kong Garden" being cited as potentially the first post-punk single. Their sound was not punk rock but could not have existed without punk preceding it. "Susie in the Banshees were their very first single Hong Kong Garden. They will forever be associated with the term post punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Personnel Crisis
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the bandsheets were formed around 1977. In 1979, during a significant personnel crisis that resulted in the group splitting into two, Budgie joined the band as drummer, approximately two years after its initial formation. "Budgie joined the band in 1979. About two years after the bandsheets were formed and during a personnel crisis that saw the group split in two."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Goth Affiliation Debate
podcast.body: The band's "Goth purity" has been debated among Goth fans, and the band themselves have, at times, distanced themselves from the Goth label. Despite this, their dark music, introspective themes, and fashion sense inextricably linked them to Goth culture, and their discovery often led listeners back to Goth. "Now there is a big debate as to the Goth purity of both the banshees and the cure among the faithful and both bands have at one time or another, distance themselves from the Goth label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Goth Archetype
podcast.body: Siouxsie Sioux, with her striking appearance of black hair, heavy mascara and eyeshadow, and soulful eyes, along with the band name "Banshees" (evoking horror), became an archetype for goths worldwide, establishing them as one of the first-generation goth bands. "Susie made for a striking figure, black hair, lots of mascara, and eyeshadow, big soulful eyes, and the name Banshees conjured up just the right amount of horror. She became an archetype for Goth's Worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Growing Influence
podcast.body: The band continued to gain popularity, and Siouxsie's fashion choices, particularly, became increasingly influential within the goth scene. "Suzy and the band she has just kept getting bigger and Suzy's fashion choices became more popular."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inclusion on Early 80s New Wave Compilations
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were featured on early 1980s New Wave compilations, showcasing the heterogeneous nature of the genre during that period. These compilations mixed various alternative and underground bands. "La refiro teníamos desde Xi Xi y me refiro como elatorio de New Wave que me tenía de Kyur, que me tenía Joe Y Division, que me tenía New Order, me tengo un poco de todo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Influence on Los Monaguillos
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were an influence on the sound of Los Monaguillos, who combined elements of Siouxsie with 70s psychedelic rock. "la banda tenía un sonido que combinaba elementos de Suxy y del rock más psicodélico de los años 70."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Influence on The Dresden Dolls
podcast.body: The Dresden Dolls are described as sounding like what would have happened if Siouxsie and the Banshees had been playing in East Berlin cabarets in 1932. "they look and sound like what might have happened had Suzy and the Banshee's been playing the Cabaret's and East Berlin in 1932."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for John Frusciante
podcast.body: John McGeoch is a significant source of inspiration for John Frusciante, particularly because of McGeoch's ability to create vastly different sounds from one song to the next. "He is a real thing for John McGocke of Suzy and the Banshees, because his sound can be so different from song to song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Key Producer for Joy Division and Post-Punk
podcast.body: Martin Hannett was a pivotal figure in the recording of Joy Division's *Unknown Pleasures* and became a key figure in the history of Post-Punk. His production and post-production work accounted for approximately 85% of the time and budget for *Unknown Pleasures*. He influenced recording methods for subsequent bands in the UK during the 1980s. "Martin Hannon acaba siendo una piza clave, y es curioso porque gracias a esto acaba siendo una piza clave durante todo lo que sería la historia del postpunk durante la carrera de la banda J-Division e incluso posiblemente de los métodos de grabación de lo que serían las bandas posteriores en el Reino Unido durante los 80."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Major 90s Goth Band
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were identified as one of the major Goth bands of the 1990s, known for their dark sounds, introspective lyrics, and a style often inspired by Gothic novels and 1800s fashions. "The major goth bands of the 90s were Bauhaus and Suzy and the Banshee's, Sisters of Mercy, and if we go back to the very beginning we'll find that Joy Division was a major influence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Peele Sessions Recordings (70s, 80s, 90s)
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were among the numerous "cool bands" invited to record live off the floor for the "Peele Sessions" at the BBC during the 70s, 80s, and 90s. These sessions provided a means for artists to be heard on the BBC, circumventing "Needle Time" restrictions on commercial records. "The Smiths, R.E.M., New Order, the Fall, Equivalent of the Buntyman, Susie the Banshee, the Bus Cox, the list is almost endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Music vs Technology Over The Years

podcast.title: Pioneering Goth Band
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were among the very first and first-generation Goth bands to emerge, helping define the genre. "Amongst the very first were Suzy in the banshees."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of Dark Wave
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were identified as a key band from which the Dark Wave genre emerged in the early 1980s, alongside The Cure. This illustrates the diversification of underground music movements away from the umbrella term "New Wave." "teníamos el Dark Wave, que es el que vendría de Xi Xi and the Bansis o el que vendría de Kyur."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Produced by Steve Lillywhite
podcast.body: Steve Lillywhite, who produced records for Siouxsie and the Banshees, sold his royalties from his work. "Steve Lillewight, who produced records for everyone from Susie in the Banshees and the psychedelic furs to the killers in Peter Gabriel and you too, sold his royalties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Queen of Goth
podcast.body: For many fans and critics, Siouxsie Sioux, the lead singer of Siouxsie and the Banshees, holds the title of the "Queen of Goth." This acknowledges her iconic status and significant influence within the Gothic rock scene that emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s. "And for many, the Queen of Goth remains Susie Sue of Susie in the Banshees."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording at Wessex Studios
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees recorded at Wessex Studios, an old church hall in North London recognized for its live sound, making it a favored location for punk and post-punk groups. "A lot of punk bands and post punk bands, like using the place, the clash and the damned and suzy and the banshees and the pretenders and the specials and generation X and the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Second Generation Goth Influence
podcast.body: The band was instrumental in carrying Goth music beyond its UK birthplace by the mid-1980s, alongside The Sisters of Mercy and The Cure. "It was carried on the wings of music, sisters of mercy, suzzy in the banshees and the cure."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shaper of Joy Division's Sound
podcast.body: Hannett was instrumental in guiding Joy Division away from their punk reminiscences towards a more experimental sound, incorporating influences from bands like Cabaret Voltaire and Can. He introduced unorthodox sounds, such as those from boxes and cans, to create the characteristic atmospheric environment of Joy Division, which complemented Ian Curtis's lyrics. "Martin Jañez lleva a la banda poco a poco a ese sonido un poco más heredado de bandas más experimentales como Cabret Volter, incluso como Cannes, que los aferca a veces incluso al Crab Rock, la música elitrónica experimental y que leis introducen sonidos como muy poco orthodoxos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Similar Direction
podcast.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees (referred to as "Suxy") are noted as a band that, alongside The Cure, was already exploring a similar musical direction to Joy Division around the time of *Unknown Pleasures*' release. This indicates a nascent shift in the music scene towards the atmospheric and reflective sounds that Joy Division would further develop. "sí que es verdad que ya teníamos abandas como de Kyura, Suxy, que estaban yendo un poco en esa dirección."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Siouxsie Sioux as Archetype
podcast.body: Singer Siouxsie Sioux's distinctive black hair, makeup, and striking appearance made her an archetype for thousands of Goth followers. "With her really striking appearance and her black hair and the makeup, Suzy became an archetype for thousands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unknown Prior to Unknown Pleasures
podcast.body: Despite his later importance, Martin Hannett was relatively unknown before working on *Unknown Pleasures*. He possessed a sophisticated and advanced vision for recording methods, both technically and artistically, which was crucial for the album's sound. "Martin Hannon cuando grabó, a no plecias no era nadie. Entonces, digamos, que fue un trabajo especialmente complejo, pero lo curioso es que Martin Hannon tenía como dos cosas que lo harían una persona clave para la grabación de este álbum."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

xref.body: Sid played drums for Siouxsie and the Banshees at their debut performance in September 1976. This was one of his early musical involvements before joining the Sex Pistols. "He was the drummer for Susie in the Banshees when they made their debut in September of 1976."

xref.title: Boston Origin and Cabaret Sound
xref.body: This two-piece group from Boston has a unique sound and look, described as if Siouxsie and the Banshees were performing in East Berlin cabarets in 1932. "There are two piece groups out of Boston and they look and sound like what might have happened had Suzy and the Banshee's been playing the Cabaret's and East Berlin in 1932."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Diverse Musical Inspirations
xref.body: His inspirations include Jimi Hendrix, Joe Strummer, Captain Beefheart, Frank Zappa, Robert Johnson, Bernard Sumner of New Order, and significantly, John McGeoch of Siouxsie and the Banshees, admired for his varied soundscapes. "And who does he look for for inspiration? Well, we talked about Hendrix, but also Joe Strummer, Captain B. Fart, Frank Zappa, loose legend Robert Johnson, Bernard Sumner of New Order."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Highly Influential British Band
xref.body: Roxy Music is considered one of the most influential British bands of all time, with a profound impact on British punks, goth kids, New Romantics, and avant-garde artists. Their influence is evident in bands like Sex Pistols, Siouxsie and the Banshees, Duran Duran, The Smiths, Talking Heads, Radiohead, and Human League. "it's not an exaggeration to say that Roxy is one of the most influential British bands of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Influences
xref.body: The band incorporated elements from Bauhaus and Siouxsie and the Banshees (referred to as "Suzy in the band she's in") and Joy Division, adding their distinctive style.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspiration for Siouxsie and the Banshees
xref.body: The Sex Pistols were ascendant and had a dedicated group of fans called the Bromley Contingent, which included Susan Ballion (later Siouxsie Sioux). Siouxsie was inspired by the Pistols to form her own punk band and later Siouxsie and the Banshees. "When the Sex Pistols were on the Ascendant, they had a group of fans that followed them everywhere. They were called the Bromley contingent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Learning from Other Guitarists (Early 2000s)
xref.body: During the period of the "By the Way" album, John Frusciante continued to learn about guitar by studying the styles of Johnny Marr of The Smiths, John McGeoch from Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Andy Partridge of XTC, seeking new chords, techniques, and textures. "He was learning even more about the guitar by studying the styles of guys like Johnny Mar of the Smiths, John from Susie in the Banshees and even Andy Partridge of XTC."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

xref.title: Punk Pioneer
xref.body: Siouxsie Sioux of Siouxsie and the Banshees was a pioneer who took advantage of punk rock values, inspiring many to express themselves regardless of background or gender. "Suzy Su, of Suzy in the Banshee's, members of the Slitz, Pauli Styrene of X-Ray Specks, Chrissy Hinder, the Pretenders, Patty Smith, and so many more. They were all pioneers and they all inspired many people, women, but also men, to do what they did."
